name: St. Patrick's Day
hook: The March 17 holiday when everyone is Irish — green, shamrocks, parades and leprechauns.

facts.label: March 17
facts.statement: It is celebrated on March 17, the anniversary of the death of a 5th-century bishop of Armagh — St. Patrick himself.

facts.label: Fifth Avenue parade
facts.statement: New York City's parade runs up Fifth Avenue; in March 2018 it celebrated its 257th anniversary. Maryville, Missouri, bills its own as "The World's Shortest" parade.

facts.label: green
facts.statement: Green is the color of the day — pancakes and even TV episodes get dyed green, and the old song celebrates "the wearin' o' the green."

facts.label: shamrock
facts.statement: The shamrock is the plant traditionally worn on the day: a trifoliate clover whose name is also a Crayola green.

facts.label: leprechaun
facts.statement: Leprechauns are the holiday's fairy folk, the quarry in the picture book "How to Catch a Leprechaun" by Adam Wallace and Andy Elkerton.

facts.label: Shamrock Shake
facts.statement: McDonald's Shamrock Shake is the minty green drink sold around the holiday; 2020 marked its 50th anniversary.

facts.label: corned beef & cabbage
facts.statement: Corned beef and cabbage is the traditional plate, while Irish stew is the "national" pot of mutton, onions and potatoes.
